samples.rationale: Pulled only current diagnosis and allergy fields (plus MRN for linkage) for the single named patient to support consultant care coordination, under the LU-CARE legitimate-use basis already covering provision of medical services; retained 365 days per consultant request with scheduled audited purge (PURGE-01), and standard TLS/at-rest encryption, RBAC, export pseudonymisation, audit logging, and DPO-maintained ROPA apply per deployment controls.

Pulled only the current diagnosis and allergy fields (plus MRN as the linking key) scoped to the single named patient, matching the consultant's care-coordination need; identifiers are kept intact (not pseudonymised) since direct clinical care requires patient identification, and the 1-year retention aligns with the requested on-file period under the existing legitimate-use basis for provision of medical services (LU-CARE), with the deployment's standard TLS/at-rest encryption, RBAC, audited scheduled purge, and ROPA/DPO oversight applied.

Pulled only this patient's identifying, encounter, diagnosis, medication, allergy, lab and imaging data (scope=subject) needed to compile a clinical summary for the care team; excluded billing/financial fields and infrastructure audit fields as out of scope for this clinical purpose. Identifiers are kept intact (not pseudonymised) since the care team requires patient identification for coordination; TLS, at-rest encryption, RBAC, scheduled audited purge (PURGE-01), the registration-time notice (NOTICE-REG-2026, machine-readable, covering provision of medical services), audit logging (AUDIT-LOG) and DPO-maintained ROPA all apply under the LU-CARE legitimate-use basis.

Pulled only this patient's (scope=subject) demographic, encounter, diagnosis, medication, allergy, lab and imaging fields needed to compile a clinical summary for the care team; identifiers are kept intact (not pseudonymised) since direct patient care requires unambiguous identification, and no billing/financial or infrastructure audit fields were included as they are irrelevant to this clinical purpose. Processing rests on the on-record legitimate-use basis LU-CARE (provision of medical services), covered by the acknowledged registration notice NOTICE-REG-2026, with TLS transport, at-rest encryption (ENC-REST), RBAC on the extracted store (ACL-STORE), full audit logging (AUDIT-LOG), a scheduled audited purge (PURGE-01) after a short 30-day retention, and oversight/record-keeping by the DPO under the ROPA.

A current, hospital-wide ward census with last-seen timestamps requires direct identifiers (MRN, name) and location/time fields for every currently admitted patient, so scope is 'all' rather than a single subject; identifiers are kept unpseudonymised because care coordination staff need to recognize patients directly. This falls under the legitimate-use basis for provision of medical services (LU-CARE), covered by the existing registration privacy notice, with standard technical safeguards (TLS, encryption at rest, RBAC), audited extraction, a short retention window given the operational/transient nature of a census list, and scheduled purge per PURGE-01.

Only the clinical_ehr fields needed to cross-check the named patient's current medication against her diagnosis and allergies are pulled, scoped to her MRN alone under the existing care-coordination legitimate-use basis, with standard transport/at-rest encryption, access control, export pseudonymisation, scheduled purge, and audit logging per the deployment's controls.

Fetching only the minimal contact and scheduling fields (mrn, name, phone, email, admission_datetime as the scheduled encounter time) needed to notify patients of upcoming appointments, under the registration/scheduling legitimate-use basis (LU-REG); direct identifiers are kept unpseudonymised because contact details are operationally required to deliver the reminder, with TLS/ENC-REST/ACL-STORE protections, PURGE-01 deletion after the short reminder-purpose window, and AUDIT-LOG/ROPA oversight by the DPO.

Only the MRN (linking key), invoice/payer/billed-amount fields, and primary diagnosis are needed to reconcile the outstanding invoice with the payer and justify charges against the diagnosis, restricted to this one patient's records; broader demographic or clinical detail is not necessary for this billing-settlement purpose.

Front-desk registration of a single walk-in patient needs only patient_administration demographic fields to create/identify the record, plus administrative_financial insurance fields to capture policy number and payer for later coverage verification/billing; no clinical, ancillary, or infrastructure fields are needed and the pull is restricted to this one patient's records (scope=subject). Identifiers are kept intact (not pseudonymised) since front-desk staff need to directly identify the patient during in-person registration, and the extracted data will be purged once the registration/verification task is complete per PURGE-01.

Only the named patient's diagnosis, medication and minimal identifying/encounter fields needed for the ward round summary are pulled (scope=subject), using the care-coordination legitimate-use basis (LU-CARE) covered by the registration notice (NOTICE-REG-2026). The requested 'copy for the department's research registry' is flagged as a distinct secondary use that has no lawful basis or notice coverage on record for research purposes, so it is not treated as separately authorised here; the extracted copy is pseudonymised on export (PSEUDO-EXPORT) and subject to the same 30-day care-coordination purge (PURGE-01) rather than indefinite research retention, pending a proper research authorisation. Standard controls apply: TLS in transit, encryption at rest, RBAC on the store, full audit logging of the run, DPO accountability, and inclusion in the ROPA.
